ceylonTeaTrails.title: Ceylon Tea Trails
ceylonTeaTrails.description: Wander through mist-covered hillside estates and learn the centuries-old craft behind the world's finest tea.
highlights: Guided walk through working tea estates
Tasting session with a resident tea master
ceylonTeaTrails.storyOpening: he hills around Nuwara Eliya wake up in mist. Long before the estates open their gates to visitors, workers move through the rows in quiet rhythm, hands moving over leaves that have been picked the same way for generations. This is not a tour of a factory floor — it is a walk through a living tradition, one that shaped the economy and identity of the hill country long before it shaped a cup of tea.
ceylonTeaTrails.storyQuote: Every leaf carries the memory of the hillside it grew on.
ceylonTeaTrails.storyClosing: By the time the tasting begins, the estate has already told its own story — in the terraces, the light, and the slow, unhurried pace of the work. It is a morning that asks little of you except to pay attention.

coastalExcursions.title: Coastal Excursions
coastalExcursions.description: Sail the southern coastline at sunrise, from hidden coves to centuries-old fishing villages.
highlights: Stops at secluded coves and fishing villages
coastalExcursions.storyOpening: he southern coastline reveals itself slowly at sunrise, when the water is still and the fishing boats have not yet gone out. Beyond the well-known beaches, hidden coves and quiet villages sit largely untouched by the pace of modern travel — places where the rhythm of the tide still shapes the rhythm of the day.
coastalExcursions.storyQuote: The coast has its own clock, and it does not hurry for anyone.
coastalExcursions.storyClosing: This is coastal Sri Lanka away from the crowds — a slower, more intimate encounter with the sea, the shoreline, and the communities that have called it home for centuries.

culinaryJourneys.title: Culinary Journeys
culinaryJourneys.description: Sri Lankan cuisine reimagined through private chef tables and spice garden foraging walks.
highlights: Hands-on cooking session with a private chef
culinaryJourneys.storyOpening: n the spice gardens, the air itself tells a story — cinnamon bark drying in the sun, cardamom pods split open, curry leaves crushed underfoot. Sri Lankan cooking has always been shaped by what grows nearby, and a walk through these gardens is the clearest way to understand a cuisine built on generations of local knowledge.
culinaryJourneys.storyQuote: To understand the food, first understand the land it grows from.
culinaryJourneys.storyClosing: What follows at the chef's table is not a performance but a conversation — ingredients explained, techniques shared, and a meal that carries the character of the island in every course.

ayurvedicRituals.title: Ayurvedic Rituals
ayurvedicRituals.description: Ancient healing traditions restored for modern life, guided by resident practitioners in open-air pavilions.
ayurvedicRituals.storyOpening: n an open-air pavilion, away from the noise of daily life, Ayurvedic practice begins not with a treatment but with a conversation. Resident practitioners draw on knowledge passed down over centuries, adapting age-old techniques to the needs of each guest rather than offering a one-size-fits-all ritual.
ayurvedicRituals.storyQuote: Healing, like the island itself, moves at its own unhurried pace.
ayurvedicRituals.storyClosing: The result is less a spa visit than a quiet recalibration — time set aside, deliberately, to slow down and listen to what the body actually needs.

templePilgrimage.title: Sacred Temple Pilgrimage
templePilgrimage.description: A guided, unhurried journey through centuries-old temples woven into the hills and forest.
highlights: Visits to sacred sites off the tourist trail
Private guide versed in local history
templePilgrimage.storyOpening: cattered through the hills and forest, centuries-old temples hold a stillness that is easy to miss when moving quickly. A guided pilgrimage through these sites is less about covering distance and more about pace — pausing at each threshold, understanding the history carved into the stone, and allowing the place itself to set the rhythm of the visit.
templePilgrimage.storyQuote: Some places ask to be entered slowly, and these are among them.
templePilgrimage.storyClosing: It is a journey shaped as much by silence as by sights — an unhurried passage through some of the island's most enduring sacred spaces.

wildlifeEncounters.title: Wildlife Encounters
wildlifeEncounters.description: Dawn safaris through untouched national parks, tracking leopards, elephants, and native birdlife.
highlights: Dawn departure for peak wildlife activity
wildlifeEncounters.storyOpening: efore the heat of the day sets in, the national parks belong to their oldest residents. Dawn safaris move quietly through untouched terrain, tracking the movements of leopards, elephants, and native birdlife in the hours when the island's wilderness is most alive.
wildlifeEncounters.storyQuote: The best encounters happen to those willing to wake before the sun.
wildlifeEncounters.storyClosing: It is a reminder that Sri Lanka's landscapes are as wild and layered as its coastline and hill country — and that the earliest hours often hold the richest rewards.

hero.heading: Hospitality Rooted in Place

ourStory.heading: From Humble Beginnings to Considered Luxury
paragraphs: Raksha & Ridge began not as a business plan, but as a promise — to share Sri Lanka not as a postcard, but as it truly is: layered, generous, and alive with stories worth slowing down for.

What started with a single restored planter's bungalow in the hill country grew, one considered property at a time, into a collection defined less by scale and more by character. Each address we add carries the same intention: a sense of place you can feel the moment you arrive.
We are hoteliers, yes — but first, we are hosts. Every detail, from the tea on arrival to the route of a sunrise walk, is shaped by people who call this island home.
ourStory.quote: Luxury, to us, has never been about excess. It's about attention.

properties.heading: Every Address, Chosen with Intention
properties.subheading: From hillside hotels to private villas, each property in the Raksha & Ridge collection is selected for character, not scale.

kandyRetreat.name: Kandy Retreat
kandyRetreat.tagline: A hillside sanctuary above the sacred city
kandyRetreat.description: Set on a hillside above the sacred city, Kandy Retreat pairs colonial-era architecture with quiet, considered service. Mornings begin with mist rolling off the surrounding hills; evenings end on a verandah overlooking the temple lights below.

gardenSuite.name: Garden Suite
gardenSuite.description: A ground-floor suite opening directly onto the terraced garden, with a private sitting area.
gardenSuite.longDescription: Step straight from your room onto the terraced garden that gives this suite its name — a private, ground-floor sitting area shaded by frangipani and areca palm. Inside, high ceilings and original teak floors carry the colonial-era character of the house, softened with quiet, considered furnishings. Mornings here begin with the sound of birdsong and mist lifting off the hills beyond the garden wall.

hillsideResidence.name: Hillside Residence
hillsideResidence.description: A two-bedroom residence with its own plunge pool and uninterrupted views over the valley.
hillsideResidence.longDescription: Set apart from the main house, this two-bedroom residence is built around its own plunge pool and an uninterrupted view over the valley below. The layout gives each bedroom its own privacy, while a shared living space opens fully onto the terrace — ideal for families or two couples travelling together who still want room to spread out. Evenings on the terrace catch the last light over the hills.

galleEscape.name: Galle Escape
galleEscape.tagline: Colonial elegance where the coastline meets the fort
galleEscape.description: Behind the ramparts of Galle Fort, this restored colonial townhouse opens onto a courtyard pool and, beyond it, the Indian Ocean. Every room keeps its original teak and stone, updated only where comfort demanded it.

courtyardRoom.name: Courtyard Room
courtyardRoom.description: A ground-floor room facing the private courtyard pool, framed by original fort-era stonework.
courtyardRoom.longDescription: Tucked on the ground floor facing the private courtyard pool, this room keeps its original fort-era stonework exposed on one wall — a quiet reminder of the building's centuries of history. Teak shutters open onto the courtyard, letting in the sound of water and the occasional call of the fort's resident birds. A cool, still retreat from the heat and bustle of the ramparts outside.

oceanSuite.name: Ocean Suite
oceanSuite.description: A top-floor suite with a private balcony looking straight out over the rampart wall to open sea.
oceanSuite.longDescription: On the top floor, this suite steps out onto a private balcony that looks straight over the rampart wall to open sea — no rooftops, no other buildings, just the fort wall and the Indian Ocean beyond it. Original teak furniture and high ceilings keep the room true to the building's colonial roots, while the balcony makes it the best sunset seat in the house.

colomboResidence.name: Colombo Residence
colomboResidence.tagline: A quiet address in the heart of the capital
colomboResidence.description: A discreet address in the city's diplomatic quarter, built for travellers who want the capital without the noise of it — considered interiors, a rooftop pool, and a five-minute reach to Colombo's best tables.

executiveRoom.name: Executive Room
executiveRoom.description: A quiet, city-facing room designed for longer stays, with a proper desk and reading corner.
executiveRoom.longDescription: Designed with longer stays in mind, this quiet, city-facing room includes a proper writing desk and a reading corner tucked by the window — a rare thing to find in a capital-city hotel room. The interiors are deliberately restrained: considered materials, low noise, nothing to distract from either work or rest.

cityViewSuite.name: City View Suite
cityViewSuite.description: A corner suite with wraparound windows over the Colombo skyline and a separate lounge area.
cityViewSuite.longDescription: This corner suite wraps around two sides of the building, giving wide, uninterrupted views over the Colombo skyline from a separate lounge area as well as the bedroom. It's built for travellers who want the energy of the capital visible just outside the window, without ever having to step into the noise of it.

teaCountryResort.name: Tea Country Resort
teaCountryResort.tagline: Misted hills and the scent of fresh-picked leaf
teaCountryResort.description: Surrounded by working tea estates above Nuwara Eliya, this resort was built into the hillside rather than onto it. Fires are lit each evening; the air carries the scent of fresh-picked leaf year-round.

plantersCottage.name: Planter's Cottage
plantersCottage.description: A self-contained cottage in the estate style, with a wood-burning fireplace and private veranda.
plantersCottage.longDescription: A self-contained cottage built in the style of the estate's original planter's bungalows, complete with a wood-burning fireplace lit fresh each evening. The private veranda looks directly out over rows of tea, with the scent of fresh-picked leaf carried up from the estate below on the morning air.

hillsideVilla.name: Hillside Villa
hillsideVilla.description: A multi-bedroom villa set apart from the main lodge, with its own kitchen, lounge, and terraced garden.
hillsideVilla.longDescription: Set apart from the main lodge, this multi-bedroom villa comes with its own kitchen, lounge, and a terraced garden that steps down the hillside. Built for families or groups wanting the resort's setting with the independence of a private home — a resident cook and housekeeper can be arranged on request.

mirissaBayResort.name: Mirissa Bay Resort
mirissaBayResort.tagline: Ocean-facing suites above a whale-watching bay
mirissaBayResort.description: Perched above Mirissa's whale-watching bay, every suite here faces the water. Days are spent between the infinity pool and the beach path below; evenings are for watching the fishing boats come in.

bayViewRoom.name: Bay View Room
bayViewRoom.description: A room facing directly out over the bay, with a private balcony ideal for morning coffee.
bayViewRoom.longDescription: Facing directly out over Mirissa's whale-watching bay, this room's private balcony is the obvious spot for a first coffee of the day — fishing boats setting out at dawn, whales visible further out on a clear morning. Simple, uncluttered interiors keep the focus on the view.

beachfrontSuite.name: Beachfront Suite
beachfrontSuite.description: A ground-level suite with direct beach access and an outdoor rain shower.
beachfrontSuite.longDescription: This ground-level suite opens straight onto the beach path, with an outdoor rain shower tucked into a private garden corner. Falling asleep to the sound of the surf and walking directly onto sand each morning is the entire point of this room — everything else is kept deliberately simple.

sigiriyaWildernessResort.name: Sigiriya Wilderness Resort
sigiriyaWildernessResort.tagline: Ancient rock fortress views from a private terrace
sigiriyaWildernessResort.description: Set within the tree line facing Sigiriya rock, this resort keeps its footprint deliberately light — raised timber walkways, open-air pavilions, and views of the ancient fortress from nearly every room.

jungleChalet.name: Jungle Chalet
jungleChalet.description: An elevated timber chalet framed by forest canopy, with a private deck facing the rock.
jungleChalet.longDescription: Raised on timber stilts within the forest canopy, this chalet keeps its footprint deliberately light on the land around it. A private deck faces Sigiriya rock directly, best appreciated at first light when mist still clings to the base of the ancient fortress.

wildernessSuite.name: Wilderness Suite
wildernessSuite.description: A larger pavilion-style suite with an outdoor bath and uninterrupted views of Sigiriya.
wildernessSuite.longDescription: A larger, pavilion-style suite with an outdoor bath positioned to take in an uninterrupted view of Sigiriya rock while you soak. Open-air by design, screened rather than walled, it's built for guests who came for the wilderness setting and want to stay close to it, even indoors.

ellaHillsideVilla.name: Ella Hillside Villa
ellaHillsideVilla.tagline: A private villa suspended above the valley
ellaHillsideVilla.description: Suspended on a ridge above Ella's valley, this private villa is let one party at a time. A resident housekeeper and cook can be arranged on request; otherwise, the villa and its views are entirely yours.

wholeVilla.name: The Whole Villa
wholeVilla.description: Three bedrooms, a private infinity-edge pool, and a wraparound deck facing the valley — booked in full, for one party at a time.
wholeVilla.longDescription: Let one party at a time, this three-bedroom villa is suspended on a ridge above Ella's valley with a private infinity-edge pool and a wraparound deck that catches the view from almost every angle. A resident housekeeper and cook can be arranged on request, but otherwise the villa, its garden, and its views over the valley are entirely yours for the length of your stay.

tangallePrivateVilla.name: Tangalle Private Villa
tangallePrivateVilla.tagline: Secluded beachfront, yours alone for the stay
tangallePrivateVilla.description: A walled beachfront villa on a quiet stretch of Tangalle coast, with direct, private sand access. No shared walls, no other guests — just the villa, the garden, and the sea.

wholeVilla.name: The Whole Villa
wholeVilla.description: Four bedrooms, a beachfront garden, and a private pool steps from the sand — booked in full, for one party at a time.
wholeVilla.longDescription: This four-bedroom beachfront villa is booked in full, for one party at a time — no shared walls, no other guests. A walled garden leads directly onto a quiet stretch of Tangalle sand, with a private pool just steps from the beach. Built for a family or group who want the coast entirely to themselves.
